tldr: This is a loose research thread on inference cost, not one event. It opened with an arXiv paper arguing that per-token billing hides cost: each token added to the KV-cache makes later tokens more expensive, so energy grows non-linearly with sequence length.
whats_new: A Nov 18 arXiv paper proposes timeout cascades to cut the GPU cost of coding agents, two days after an open-source benchmark compared OSS inference vendors on cost and latency.
why_it_matters: Long-context and agentic workloads cost more than flat per-token prices suggest, so vendor choice and agent run limits are cost levers, not just latency settings.

beats.headline: Paper argues tokens are not equally expensive
beats.summary: KV-cache growth makes later tokens cost more energy than earlier ones.

beats.headline: Open-source benchmark compares OSS inference vendors on cost and latency
Timeout cascades proposed to cut coding-agent compute
beats.summary: Targets agent runs, one of the heaviest GPU consumers.

open_questions: Do any inference providers price long-context tokens to reflect KV-cache cost?
How much do timeout cascades save on a public coding-agent benchmark, and at what pass-rate loss?
Do the inference-bench vendor rankings hold across model sizes and context lengths?
take_for_builders: Measure your agent's cost per completed task across context lengths before picking a vendor, and test a timeout cap on long-running agent attempts.
